The guide's package contents say the unit \"includes 2 PSUs\".","kind":"base"}},"description":"48 x 1G RJ-45 PoE plus 6 x 1G/10G SFP+ 1RU access switch, sold as the EPS122 and stamped AS4625-54P. All ports on the front in TWO ROWS OF TWENTY-FOUR COLUMNS ganged in three blocks of eight, numbered 1-48, with the SFP+ uplinks numbered 49-54. THE RJ-45 ROW IS TWO PoE CLASSES AND THE PANEL SAYS WHICH: ports 1-40 at 30 W and ports 41-48 at 90 W, the latter marked with an orange band and legended \"0.53A Max/Port1-40, 1.85A Max/Port41-48\". An RJ-45 management jack over an RJ-45 console, a Micro-USB storage port, a Reset button and six status lamps. TWO HOT-SWAPPABLE SUPPLIES AND THREE FIXED FANS on the rear. Its sibling edgecore/eps121 is the same chassis without PoE.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front"],"wanted":"WHAT IS PRINTED UNDER EVERY PORT COLUMN. Both instruments show a row of small light marks about 1.5 mm across below the RJ-45 block, one per column, and NEITHER RESOLVES THEM - the guide's line art at 5.03 px/mm and the datasheet photograph at 9.07 px/mm both reduce them to blur at nine times magnification. They are either a second port numbering or a second lamp row, and the face is modelled without them rather than with a guess. One enlargement of the lower edge closes this.","what":"the-row-under-the-ports"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"HOW DEEP THE THREE FAN GUARDS ARE. `edgecore/eps-fan-fixed@1` carries a 10 mm vent depth and it is an estimate: the fans are fixed, no FRU figure exists for them, and neither document dimensions the rear. The guards' FACE geometry is measured - 25.5 x 15.9 on a 47.8 pitch, agreeing between the two models' elevations to 0.2 mm - so only the depth is open.","what":"fixed-fan-depth"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"2+1","redundancy-note":"\"2+1 fixed redundant fans\", from the Overview callouts of both models. **THEY ARE NOT FRUs AND THERE ARE NO BAYS** - the guide's FRU Replacement section covers the supplies only, and there is no latch, handle or seam to draw. So the three fans are PLACED rather than bayed, and the 2+1 counts rotors that nobody swaps. A census that asks whether this figure fills its bays will find none, and that is correct."},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Part"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Point"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the out-of-band cluster - an RJ-45 management jack over an RJ-45 console jack, a Micro-USB storage port and the Reset button. The guide legends the management jack's own lamps \"Left (link), Right (activity)\".","role":"management","term":"Port"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"\"Redundant hot-swappable AC PSUs\", two bays, and the guide's Connect Power step says \"Install one or two AC PSUs in the device, if they are not already installed in the factory\" - so one will run the machine and the second is the redundancy."},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"rj45-1g":{"attrs":{"media":"rj45","poe":"802.3at 30 W","speed":"1g"},"description":"the forty-eight 1G RJ-45 ports, two rows of twenty-four columns ganged in three blocks of eight, numbered 1-48 down each column. ALL FORTY-EIGHT ARE PoE and they are TWO CLASSES: \"40 x 1G RJ-45 PoE ports (30 W per port)\" and \"8 x 1G RJ-45 PoE ports (90 W per port)\", which the panel's own legend resolves to ports 1-40 and 41-48.","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"rj45-poe-hi":{"attrs":{"media":"rj45","poe":"802.3bt 90 W","speed":"1g"},"description":"ports 41-48, the EIGHT 90 W PoE ports. They are the same jacks in the same ganged row as ports 1-40 and differ only in what they may deliver, which the panel prints beside them - \"1.85A Max/Port41-48\" - and marks with an orange band. The Overview callouts list them separately from the other forty for the same reason.","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp","speed":"10g"},"description":"the six 1G/10G SFP+ uplinks, three stacked pairs at the right of the port wall, numbered 49-54 into the same sequence as the RJ-45 ports. `index-origin` is 1 because the schema allows 0 or 1 and nothing else; the 49 the panel prints is carried by each port's own `rel-pos`, which is where the panel's numbering belongs.","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"AS4625-54P","name":"eps122","portfolio":{"family":"Access Switch","line":"Enterprise","series":"EPS122"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"gate-1":{"confidence":"measured","note":"SIX INSTRUMENTS, AND ALL SIX SAY THE HEIGHT IS 44.45 mm RATHER THAN THE SPECIFICATION TABLE'S 44. The guide's four elevations read 2215x224, 2213x224, 2213x224 and 2219x224 px; the two datasheet front photographs 3991x404 and 3998x408. Against 440 x 44 they come out -1.116%, -1.205%, -1.205%, -0.938%, -1.213% and -2.010%. Against 440 x 44.45 - true 1RU - they come out -0.105%, -0.195%, -0.195%, +0.076%, -0.203% and -1.008%. Six failures become six passes and the spread collapses by an order of magnitude, so the table's \"44\" is a rounding and the drawings are to 44.45. EVERY y MEASUREMENT IN THIS FILE USES THE 44.45 SCALE. On a 44 mm face the difference is half a millimetre at the bottom edge, which is the size of the features being measured. `chassis.height` still records the vendor's published 44: this is a drawing-scale fact, not a dimension change. WHICH INSTRUMENT FOR WHICH JOB, and this one is the opposite of the DCS520's. The guide's LINE ART is the geometry instrument even at 5.03 px/mm, and the datasheet PHOTOGRAPHS at 9.07 px/mm are for detail and colour - because the ganged-pitch fit below comes out with an rms of 0.082 mm on the line art and 0.74 mm on the photograph. White RJ-45 bezels are soft at 9 px/mm; a drawn edge is not."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE POE MACHINE. \"AS4625-54P: Low-line (90-136 VAC): 2000 Watts max. High-line (180-264 VAC): 2400 Watts max.\" power consumption at 25 C; a per-PSU system input rating of \"100-120 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 12 A max. / 200-240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 8.5 A max.\"; and a PoE budget of \"Low-line: 850 W for 1 PSU, 1850 W for 2 PSUs. High-line: 1050 W for 1 PSU, 1920 W for 2 PSUs\". THE PER-SUPPLY OUTPUT IS NOWHERE STATED and is not invented - the supplies' own contract omits `power-output-w` rather than guess it. THE POE SPLIT IS PRINTED ON THE PANEL. The guide's right-hand enlargement shows the legend \"PoE Output: 57V ... Max., 0.53A Max/Port1-40, 1.85A Max/Port41-48\", and the Overview callouts match it: \"40 x 1G RJ-45 PoE ports (30 W per port)\" and \"8 x 1G RJ-45 PoE ports (90 W per port)\". So ports 41-48 are the 90 W ones, and the panel marks them with an orange band."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"ONE QUICK START GUIDE COVERS BOTH MODELS and it is staged twice, byte-identical - md5 c81e696fe001edaa86961a6660f8da00, 1343641 bytes. Its title page reads \"Ethernet Switch AS4625-54T | AS4625-54P\" and its package contents \"AS4625-54T/AS4625-54P (includes 2 PSUs)\". Each model additionally has its own four-page datasheet with its own photographs of both faces. THE GUIDE DISCLAIMS ITS OWN DRAWINGS - \"Note: The drawings in this document are for illustration only and may not match your particular model\" - and on this family that is not boilerplate to ignore: see the status-lamp note below."},"the-management-cluster":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AT THE RIGHT, STACKED: an RJ-45 management jack over an RJ-45 console jack - the panel legends them \"(up) Mgmt\" and \"Console\" - with a MICRO-USB storage port below under a \"USB\" label. Both jacks read rows 18.75 and 30.86, which is the RJ-45 block's own row pitch to 0.12 mm, so they sit in the same stack the traffic ports do. THE MICRO-USB IS WORTH NAMING because the third member of this shell family does not have one: the EPS112's guide lists a full-size \"USB storage port\" where this one lists a \"Micro-USB storage port\". The clusters are not interchangeable between the three."},"the-port-wall":{"confidence":"measured","note":"FORTY-EIGHT RJ-45 IN TWO ROWS OF TWENTY-FOUR COLUMNS, ganged in THREE BLOCKS OF EIGHT. Fitted by least squares over all twenty-four columns with a per-block offset, on the mean of both rows' openings: **pitch 14.0158, gutter 6.4058, first centre 15.425, rms 0.082 mm, max residual 0.17**. Rows read y 14.96-22.78 and 27.29-34.66 on the photograph, centres 18.87 and 30.97, so a row pitch of 12.10. THEN SIX SFP+ AS THREE STACKED PAIRS at x 370.20, 387.98 and 405.75 - a pitch of 17.78 - with rows at 16.67 and 32.25. The SFP rows are further apart than the RJ-45 rows because that block has a divider band between its cages where the RJ-45 block has none; both were measured, neither was assumed from the other. NUMBERING IS ONE SEQUENCE ACROSS BOTH FAMILIES: RJ-45 1-48, SFP+ 49-54, legended `N (up)(down) N+1` above each column."},"the-status-lamps-and-what-the-shared-guide-cannot-settle":{"confidence":"measured","note":"SIX LAMPS IN TWO ROWS OF THREE, on a black plate beside the Edge-core logo and the model text, with a Reset button between them. Measured on the guide's Status LEDs enlargement, calibrated on the port columns it draws (`1 (up)(down) 2` through `11 (up)(down) 12`, whose centres this file already knows exactly) at 22.62 px/mm - four and a half times the elevation: lamp columns at x 53.2, 61.0 and 68.9, rows at y 4.50 and 7.90, which the elevation's own label baselines independently confirm at 4.46 and 7.98. THE LEGEND, transcribed from the guide: System green = OK, amber = fault detected; PSU1/2 green = OK, amber = fault; FAN green = OK, amber = fault; LOC blinking amber = switch locator; PoE green = OK, amber = near PoE budget. THE ENLARGEMENT IS OF THIS MODEL - it is captioned AS4625-54P - so the six lamps and their legends are read rather than inherited. Its sibling the EPS121 is the one with the doubt: it has no PoE, and no enlargement of its own."},"why-this-is-its-own-device":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"ONE GUIDE COVERS THE 54T AND THE 54P, SO THE QUESTION HAD TO BE ASKED. `docs/what-a-configuration-cannot-say.md` answers it in one sentence - a configuration can say what OCCUPIES a bay, but not what is TRUE of a part - and records that a config-scoped DEVICE attr is still open, filed as `config-scoped-device-attrs` on cisco/asr-9001. These two differ in exactly that forbidden way: weight 5.8 kg against 6.6, power consumption 150 W against 2400, per-PSU input 4 A against 12 A. The supplies really are different parts - 50.4 mm wide against 62.3, and the PoE one carries a fan - which a configuration could have expressed through `bays`; the weight and the consumption are device attrs, which it could not. And the 54P's RJ-45 row is TWO port groups where the 54T's is one, which changes the shape of the face rather than what fills it. See roc-ops/Portrayal#335 for the full working."}},"references":[{"title":"Edgecore AS4625-54T | AS4625-54P Quick Start Guide"},{"title":"Edgecore EPS122 / AS4625-54P Datasheet"}],"version":"1.0.1","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Not drawn by any staged source.
